name: _test_optional_floatlist
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_test_optional_floatlist(Tensor values, float[]? addends) -> Tensor. This representative signature is not exclusive; the original Gems pytest owns and defines the full contract of overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and tests must never be narrowed to this one signature. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: "aten::_test_optional_floatlist(Tensor values, float[]? addends) -> Tensor"; "aten::_test_optional_floatlist.out(Tensor values, float[]? addends, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!)". Semantics (from the tests): a CPU-only ATen test helper whose operands are real CPU tensors. With addends=None it returns the operand tensor itself (same object, dtype, shape and strides) for any storage dtype and rank. With a float[] addends it returns a fresh buffer that adds the host list elementwise to rank-1 float32 values; the schema requires len(addends) >= values.numel() (extra entries are ignored, a tuple is accepted like a list). The pytest exercises the missing derivative through the addends=None call form, asserting that torch.autograd.grad raises 'derivative for aten::_test_optional_floatlist is not implemented'. addends has no schema default, so the argument is always required even though its value may be None, and both positional None and addends=None keyword forms are valid. The .out overload (not expressed by this representative signature) writes through the caller's buffer, returns and aliases that buffer, mutates it, resizes a zero-element buffer in place, and rejects mismatched buffer dtypes; those overload-dependent effects are covered by the pytest, not by this model.
